cases.statement: One person, reported twice: the case report (31781017) and a review table row (36088400 Table 1 #16) citing it as reference [30]. The pipeline merged both rows into one identity.

people.label: patient
people.key_phenotypes: adult onset of dysarthria and wide-based unstable gait during chemotherapy for ovarian cancer; spastic tetraparesis, nystagmus, dysphagia, ataxia; marked medulla-to-upper-cervical-cord atrophy (tadpole-like); later palatine tremor; respiratory involvement

quotes.quote: A Caucasian woman, born in 1960, was diagnosed with ovarian cancer (pT3cN1G3) in 2008 and treated with surgery, carboplatin, and paclitaxel.
Genetic analysis of the GFAP gene detected a heterozygous mutation in exon 1 (c.219G>C), resulting in an amino acid exchange at codon 73 from methionine to isoleucine (p.M73I) (Figure 2A).
During the second and third chemotherapy cycles (seven cycles in total), her relatives noted onset of an imperfect utterance of words and an unstable and wide-base gait.

On admission to our hospital in 2014, neurological examination revealed slurred speech, mild dysphagia, spastic tetraparesis involving mainly the left side, increased muscle stretch reflexes and Babinski sign, bilateral horizontal nystagmus, dysmetria, ataxia, and moderate dysdiadochokinesia.
Cerebral and spinal MRI showed marked atrophy from the medulla oblongata to the upper cervical spinal cord with dorsal enhancement.
The neurological examination also showed the onset of a palatine tremor (at ≈2 Hz) and square waves jerks.

phenotype_specificity.statement: Authors judge the clinical and radiological features suggestive of AxD; paraneoplastic antibodies were negative and CSF normal. Only GFAP was sequenced; no other genes are reported as tested.

quotes.quote: Overall, the clinical and radiological features were suggestive of AxD.
No paraneoplastic antibodies (anti-Yo, -Hu -Ri) were detected in serum or CSF.
Hematologic screening and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) examination were normal.
The nine exons, and corresponding exon–intron boundaries of the GFAP gene, isoform 1 (RefSeq NM_002055.5) were amplified and sequenced as described previously (8).

segregation.statement: No relatives tested. Father had a gait disturbance (possible post-polio syndrome) and a 56-year-old sister had a gait disturbance; no further family information.

quotes.quote: Review of the family history disclosed that her father had a gait disturbance, diagnosed as a possible post-polio syndrome, and her 56-year-old sister had a gait disturbance, as well.
No further family information was available.

de_novo.statement: Parental testing could not be performed.

quotes.quote: Since parental screening could not be performed, an either “de novo” or inherited nature of the p.M73I mutation remains to be defined.

functional.statement: Construct assay in transiently transfected HeLa cells (not patient cells): M73I-GFAP formed cytoplasmic aggregates in 100% of 148 transfected cells versus 0.00% for wild type (n = 170); R239C used as a known-variant comparator.

quotes.quote: Wild-type GFAP assembled into bundled filaments that extended throughout the cytoplasm; the proportion of cells showing GFAP aggregates from the transfected wild-type-GFAP was 0.00%.
Both M73I-GFAP and R239C-GFAP failed to assemble into filaments; instead, they formed clusters of cytoplasmic aggregates.

The proportion of cells transfected with M73I-GFAP and R239C-GFAP showing GFAP aggregates was 100% (n = 170 HeLa cells transfected with wild-type-GFAP, n = 148 cells transfected with M73I-GFAP, n = 172 cells transfected with R239C-GFAP, Chi-square 490.0, df 2, p < 0.0001, Figure 2B).

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Missense, p.(Met73Ile), exon 1. Other missense changes at Met73 are reported by the authors; the review paper states GFAP disease variants act by gain of function.

quotes.quote: Three different missense mutations at the same residue of the GFAP protein have been previously reported: p.M73R, p.M73K, and p.M73T.
Previous papers showed that AxD-associated mutations perturb IF assembly (1).
Gain of function variants in GFAP are associated with different forms of AxD as a neurodegenerative disorder with autosomal dominant inheritance mode [3, 24].

computational_predictions.statement: GERP++ 2.26 at Met73; unnamed in-silico analyses via VarSome reported as predicting a damaging effect.

quotes.quote: Consistent with highly conserved Met73 (GERP^++ = 2.26)
Coherent with the role the present GFAP mutation can play, several in silico analyses have predicted the p.M73I substitution to be pathogenic (https://varsome.com/).

population_data_in_papers.statement: Not found in gnomAD exomes (125,748) or genomes (15,708), as stated by the authors.

quotes.quote: the present substitution to an isoleucine residue was not found in 125,748 GnomAD exomes and 15,708 GnomAD genomes (https://gnomad.broadinstitute.org/)

authors_classification.statement: Authors call it a novel disease-causing mutation (title and text); no ACMG criteria stated.

quotes.quote: A Novel Mutation of GFAP Causing Adult-Onset Alexander Disease
Genetic analysis disclosed a novel missense mutation in the GFAP gene (see Genetic Findings).

concerns: Same person in two papers: 36088400 Table 1 row 16 cites reference [30] = PMID 31781017; already merged under AXD-ID0128. Count once.
The review row gives age 49, while the case report's abstract describes a 54-year-old woman born in 1960; the ages refer to different time points or one is in error.
Onset during platinum-based chemotherapy for metastatic ovarian cancer; the authors discuss a possible trigger. Paraneoplastic antibodies were negative.
Father and sister with gait disturbance were not tested.
Functional assay in HeLa cells with an overexpression construct, not astrocytes or patient cells.
notes_for_panel: Adult-onset single case with a construct assay and a gnomAD absence statement. No parental or family testing.
